 • Hide a small, antique key or a replica “mysterious” artifact (like a miniature compass or magnifying glass). Attach a tiny card that hints at a hidden lock or secret room.
 • Consider integrating items that tie into a story you create for your Airbnb, such as “The key that unlocks the legend.”

 • Scatter a few uniquely shaped puzzle pieces around the house. Guests must collect all of them to solve a final puzzle.
 • Add small tokens, such as emblematic symbols (a coin, a charm, or a uniquely carved marker) that indicate parts of a larger hidden message.

 • Consider placing a UV-reactive message behind a mirror or under a painting; guests could use a small UV pen (provided in a “starter kit”) to reveal hidden hints.

 • At the end of the scavenger hunt, have a small treasure chest or box that contains a quirky prize or a themed souvenir (like a locally made trinket or a “certificate” declaring them a master sleuth).
 • This final reward ties in all the clues and provides a memorable takeaway from their adventure.

Tips for Success:
• Keep Clues Balanced: Make sure clues are engaging yet solvable so guests don’t feel frustrated.
• Maintain the Story: Create a loose narrative or backstory that links the hidden items, so the hunt feels like an unfolding mystery.
• Respect Privacy: Ensure that hidden items don’t disrupt personal spaces (like inside guests’ suitcases) or essentials. Focus on common areas and outdoor public spaces.
• Provide a Starter Guide: A small “adventurer’s kit” left in the main area with instructions and a hint on how to begin can both intrigue and help guests unfamiliar with scavenger hunts.

By blending physical clues with a bit of storytelling and creative hiding spots, your Airbnb can turn a routine stay into a memorable, interactive adventure that guests will love sharing with their friends. Happy hosting!
